original_query: select deptno c, min(y), max(z) z, sum(r), sum(m) n, sum(x) sal from (    select deptno, ename, sum(sal) x, max(sal) z,       min(sal) y, count(hiredate) m, count(mgr) r    from emp group by deptno, ename) t group by deptno
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    deptno AS c,
    MIN(sal) AS "min",
    MAX(sal) AS z,
    COUNT(mgr) AS "sum",
    COUNT(hiredate) AS n,
    SUM(sal) AS sal
FROM emp
GROUP BY deptno;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Eliminate the inner GROUP BY (deptno, ename) subquery. The outer aggregates over inner aggregates are associative: sum-of-sums = SUM(sal), min-of-mins = MIN(sal), max-of-maxs = MAX(sal), and sum-of-counts = COUNT(mgr)/COUNT(hiredate). A single-level GROUP BY deptno is exactly equivalent.
Collapse the two-level aggregation into one aggregation over emp grouped by deptno, avoiding a high-cardinality hash aggregate/sort on (deptno, ename) over 45M rows. No CTE is needed.
No joins are present; this category is not applicable. The main win comes from removing the redundant intermediate aggregation.
